A comparison illustration showing two scenes side-by-side. Left: Jesus standing before Caiaphas, the High Priest tearing his rich robes in anger, surrounded by bearded Jewish elders (Sanhedrin). Right: Jesus standing before Pontius Pilate on a Roman judgment seat; Pilate is washing his hands in a bronze bowl held by a servant, while an angry crowd shouts below.

A solemn scene depicting the burial of Jesus. The body of Jesus, wrapped in white linen bands, is being gently carried by two bearded men (Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus) into a dark cave-like tomb carved into a rocky hillside. A large, heavy, round stone sits on a track beside the entrance, ready to be rolled into place. Two women in modest ancient dress watch quietly from a short distance.
